newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thai Airways cargo strike may end Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways cargo strike may end Nov 6.

text.p: Thai Airways International Plc expects a cargo workers strike in Bangkok to end on Wednesday, November 6, the airline's cargo sales manager Germany, Guillermo Valencia, said.
Airline officials in Bangkok had informed him flight operations would be back to normal Wednesday, he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Nearly 1,000 Thai Airways cargo handling workers were on strike for the second day on Tuesday at Bangkok's Don Muang Airport, paralysing cargo movements of the national carrier and many Asian airlines.
They were protesting at plans to separate Thai Airways cargo operations into a separate company, in which the airline would only hold a 40 per cent stake, over fears of potential job losses.
Valencia said the strike had caused up to 50 tonnes of freight due to be transported between Thailand and Germany to be left standing in airport facilities.
"There are clients here in Germany waiting for their freight," he said.

A joint Thai-Lufthansa freighter left full on Monday for Bangkok but no cargo could be loaded on to a Thai Airways passenger flight from Frankfurt on Tuesday because it would not be unloaded in Bangkok, he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
